text:
B: Hello! Oh there you are. I'm Nicola, hiya.
A: Hello, duck, Graham. Can you hear me alright? I've got the volume up full here.
B: Loud and clear! Where are you then?
A: Beeston, just outside Nottingham. You?
B: Frome, in Somerset. Sort of near Bath, if that helps.
A: Oh, I know Frome. Went through it on the train once, years ago. Lovely little town, all them steep streets.
B: Proper steep, yeah, my calves are ruined. So what do you do, Graham?
A: I'm a postie. Well, part-time, early shifts, walking round in Chilwell. Up at half four. I did nearly thirty years as a civil engineer before that, highways, drainage, project management, and then I sort of... decided I'd had enough of it, you know. So now I walk about twenty thousand steps a day and nobody rings me about culverts.
B: Twenty thousand! That's amazing. I'm lucky if I do parkrun without walking half of it.
A: Do you do parkrun? I do Beeston. Careful pace, mind, I'm not breaking any records.
B: Saturdays, when I can be bothered. I chat at the back with my mate. Does it count if you walk half of it, do you reckon?
A: No, see, it counts. It's five K, you got round. That's the whole point of it. Anyone who says otherwise wants a word with themselves.
B: Ha, I'm telling my friend that. I'm a dental hygienist, by the way, two days a week at a practice in Frome.
A: Oh, right. I'll keep me mouth shut then. I'm terrible for flossing.
B: Everyone says that! I never tell anyone off, honestly. Have you got a dog? I've got a Jack Russell, Biscuit, she won't go out if it's raining.
A: No dog of me own, but there's a springer on my round who waits at the gate every morning. I save him a treat. Not your Biscuit.
B: Ha! Do you live on your own then?
A: I do, yeah. Separated a couple of years. I've got two grown-up kids, son in Nottingham who I see most Sundays, and me daughter's up in Leeds. Don't see her as much as I'd like.
B: Mine's in Cardiff. Megan, she's twenty, at uni. And Alfie's fifteen, still at home, eats everything in the fridge.
A: Fifteen, oh, I remember that. We used to do a big shop and it'd be gone by Tuesday.
B: Exactly that. What do you do with yourself then, apart from the round?
A: Oh, I keep busy. Watercolours at an evening class, pub quiz Tuesdays, I'm learning Italian on Duolingo, four hundred and something days. Did a rail trip round northern Italy last year, had it all on a spreadsheet, every train, every backup.
B: A spreadsheet! I'd be hopeless, I just go wherever my friends have booked. I did Lisbon with the girls like that.
A: Lisbon's on the list. Is it as hilly as they say?
B: Worse than Frome! But proper lovely. The custard tarts, you know? And everyone was so friendly.
A: That'll do me. And Forest are... well, we won't talk about Forest.
B: I don't follow football really, I watch the rugby in the pub for the atmosphere.
A: Rugby. Oh dear. We'll have to agree to disagree there, duck.
B: Ha! Fair enough. Do you paint the canals then? I bet you do.
A: How'd you guess? There's one behind me, actually, Beeston lock, it's a bit crooked on the wall, I keep meaning to...
